body:
Let me provide more context.

In the existing script for Linux, locations of the tools to use were hard-coded and concentrated in the top section of the shell script as simple assignments of static strings that the user was expected to change. This worked across upgrades, as the paths were not version-dependent. On Windows, however, the default install paths include a version number, so I added auto-detection to pick the highest installed version in the default location to avoid breaking on upgrades.

That change had an unintended side effect: it made it less obvious how to override the paths for non-standard installations. Typically, users expect only simple string assignments at the top of a script to be user-configurable, and the version-finding block of code violated this expectation. So now I need to solve both the original "be robust to version upgrades" problem and the new usability requirement.

Proposal: At the top, let me add some variables that allow users to hard-code their tool location. If they are set to anything other than "auto", do not run the search for the highest-versioned tools in their default location.

@topoldo would this work for you?
